entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Covid-19 waking up, Cyclospora marches on, and measles is close to hitting a milestone. Here’s your disease “weather” report, covering where Covid-19 is waking up and how measles is about to make headlines (again). There is also a spotlight on the ongoing *Cyclospora* outbreak, which deserves an award for the most opaque and confusing outbreak ever, leaving consumers in the dark. Here’s what’s going on and, most importantly, what it means for you. **What this means for you:** If you’re over 65 and never got your spring Covid-19 vaccine, the time is now. As of July 19, 2026, the U.S. has reported 2,278 measles cases this year—already nearing the total for all of 2025 with five months still to go. Either the contaminated food works its way out of circulation, or it takes a few weeks, the temperatures get cool, and the parasites no longer mature on produce (basically killing themselves off.) It’s hard to tell from the data alone if this outbreak is coming to a close given that it’s significantly delayed.

entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Senate Health Committee Delays Vote to Confirm HHS Nominee. July 23, 2026, 1:55 PM UTC. The Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee delayed the vote on a top Health and Human Services nominee Thursday, just hours before the panel planned to advance his nomination. Sean Kaufman, President Donald Trump’s nominee to lead the health agency’s Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response, faced questions during his confirmation hearing earlier this month over his past questioning of the safety of vaccines. He attempted to walk back some of his comments during questions from senators. “There are ongoing conversations with the administration on the path forward for Mr. Kaufman’s nomination,” said a HELP committee spokesperson. ## Learn more about Bloomberg Law or Log In to keep reading:. ### See Breaking News in Context. entity_ranked_evidence.title: Workforce Preparation for Fall Immunization Season Starts Now - Pharmacy Times
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: * July 2026 Influenza Guide for Pharmacists. # Workforce Preparation for Fall Immunization Season Starts Now. Author(s)*Troy Trygstad, PharmD, PhD, MBA, Pharmacy Times Editor in Chief*. Influenza vaccination preparation should be on the docket for any pharmacy, and it isn’t too early to start now. The annual sprint (or is it a marathon?), which spans from roughly September to early December, isn’t that far off, and now is the time to take a few key next steps. If you don’t already have a system that automatically checks your state’s immunization registry for patient gaps in influenza and COVID-19 vaccinations for other nonseasonal vaccination opportunities, ask for it now. Vaccine spreads are more generous than average, and administration fees are billable for most patients.1 With $40,000 to $90,000 on the table for the average pharmacy, it’s worth spending a few hours prior to the dog days of summer to prepare.2.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: Is COVID returning? Summer uptick of virus may have begun in California - Los Angeles Times
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: Summer uptick of virus may have begun in California. COVID-19 is on the upswing in California and across a swath of the West and the South, a sign that the virus may be starting its seasonal summer uptick. Wastewater concentrations are also increasing,” according to Grant Boyken, a spokesperson for the California Department of Public Health. That’s lower than at the same time in the prior two years, but it’s still an increase from a month ago, when the test positivity rate was 1.15%. According to health officials and experts, it wouldn’t be surprising for a summer increase in COVID to begin now. The test positivity rate is also increasing in Orange County, with 3% of COVID tests coming back positive for the week that ended July 11, up from 1.3% a month ago. In Northern California, wastewater detections and the COVID test positivity rate are up in San Francisco, the city’s Department of Public Health said.
